baseline.head: 41d9f55270581d9660664f6c23c65ab0d7af0a4a
baseline.scopeNote: The baseline predates R0-R2 normalization edits. Existing modified and untracked work remains user-owned and must not be reset, cleaned, committed, pushed, or represented as normalization-only work.

included: Exact classification of safe non-runtime cleanup targets
Read-only dependency, build, test, and CI reachability audit for R3 candidates
excluded: Device writes, flight, HIL execution, capability activation, deployment, commit, push, or release
Customer data, credentials, licensed SDK contents, or production resources

actions.rationale: The files were ignored, unreferenced root captures without a source revision or durable acceptance record. Archiving preserves bytes while removing root ambiguity.
actions.replacement: Future acceptance captures live with a dated acceptance or audit record; these files are historical only.
actions.rollback: Move each artifact from the recorded destination back to its exact source path after verifying the recorded SHA-256; no byte transformation is allowed.

actions.rationale: These ignored root paths are regenerable CTest, type-check, browser, test, and lint output and are neither source nor durable evidence.
actions.replacement: Regenerate only through the owning CTest, Mypy, browser, Pytest, or Ruff command; durable evidence must be recorded separately.
actions.rollback: Rerun the owning tool. The deleted caches are not a recoverable evidence source and no private/customer originals are included.

actions.rationale: These ignored paths can contain owner-private original media and HIL evidence. Normalization has no authority to inspect, move, rewrite, archive, or delete them.
actions.replacement: None; the originals remain in their owner-private canonical locations.

actions.rationale: Pinned reference implementations are read-only inputs to adoption decisions and are neither product authority nor runtime dependencies.
actions.replacement: None; product implementations must remain in KSI-owned runtime modules.

actions.rationale: A single routing index now distinguishes active authority/current state from superseded or historical evidence without rewriting the historical files.
actions.replacement: docs/DOCUMENT_STATUS.md is the routing index; product authority remains in its original canonical files.
actions.rollback: Remove the routing index references and revert only the R0-R2 authority/status annotations; do not delete historical documents.

actions.owner: Product design and Dashboard audit owners
actions.rationale: Existing canonical homes already separate active prototypes, adopted design constraints, durable audits, and historical captures; the structure map makes that boundary explicit.
actions.replacement: Use the canonical homes listed in REPOSITORY_STRUCTURE.md for all new assets.
actions.rollback: No runtime or active design source was moved; remove only the routing text if the decision is superseded.

actions.rationale: The standard monorepo categories are structurally useful but several child names do not reveal the human product responsibility, deployability, or evidence status. Parent indexes and one evidence-backed audit make the distinction explicit without risky runtime renames.
actions.replacement: Each parent README gives the current human product meaning; proposed runtime path changes remain non-authoritative R3 candidates in the naming audit.
actions.rollback: Remove only the additive index/audit documents and their links; no runtime path was renamed or moved.

actions.rationale: The local virtual environment is reproducible from the pinned Python version, pyproject.toml, and uv.lock, but removing it would disrupt the active WIP validation environment without improving repository source structure.
actions.replacement: Recreate in the same ignored path with uv sync --locked only when the operator elects to rebuild the environment.
actions.rollback: No operation was performed; if separately removed, recreate from .python-version, pyproject.toml, and uv.lock.

actions.rationale: This ignored directory can contain active local journals, keys, and OIDC state. Size or hidden naming is not proof that it is disposable, and R0-R2 has no authority to inspect or rewrite it.
actions.replacement: None in R0-R2; owner-scoped backup/retention or isolated recreation requires a separate local-runtime cleanup decision.

actions.rationale: Ignored weights and runtime artifacts can be large but are bound to model registry lineage and licensing. R0-R2 records their canonical local location without uploading, moving, or deleting them.
actions.replacement: The tracked model registry and fetch tools describe reproducible artifacts; local bytes remain operator-managed and are never product authority by presence alone.

actions.rationale: The ignored source grid is an operator-acquired licensed/provenanced original used to regenerate the tracked runtime conversion. It is not a disposable build cache and R0-R2 cannot redistribute, archive, or delete it.
actions.replacement: The acquisition record and conversion tool preserve lineage; the licensed raw bytes remain only in their existing local owner path.

actions.owner: Repository governance and local agent-tool owners
actions.rationale: These paths have different roles: local agent configuration, session continuity, tool state, and helper-owned durable goal/risk ledgers. Hidden names do not make them interchangeable or disposable.
actions.replacement: .ksi remains helper-owned durable state; .ai remains non-authoritative continuity/evidence; the other directories remain local tool configuration.
actions.rollback: No directory move or deletion was performed; goal-ledger changes are made only through the registered helper.

actions.rationale: These ignored files are machine- or device-specific configuration and can contain local endpoints or vendor provisioning values. They are not repository source or cleanup-safe generated output, so R0-R2 records their ownership without reading, moving, hashing, or deleting their contents.
actions.replacement: Tracked example files define shape only; real values stay in the existing ignored owner paths and must be recreated through the approved secret/provisioning workflow.
actions.rollback: No operation was performed and no secret value was inspected or copied.

actions.rationale: The fetched PSDK tree is an ignored, pinned, licensed build input. It is not a reference repository or KSI-owned source, and deleting or relocating it is outside normalization authority.
actions.replacement: Re-fetch only from the pinned lock and approved vendor source; never copy vendor runtime code into KSI-owned modules.

actions.owner: Dashboard, design, Edge, and local tool owners
actions.rationale: These ignored dependency trees, builds, prototype outputs, test results, and caches already live below their owner. They are not product authority or durable acceptance evidence, but bulk deletion could disrupt the preserved WIP and is not required by the root-hygiene completion gate.
actions.replacement: Regenerate below the same owning module. Durable captures or test evidence must be promoted explicitly to a dated acceptance/audit record with source revision.
actions.rollback: No operation was performed; an owner-approved future cleanup may delete exact generated paths and regenerate them from locked manifests/build commands.

actions.owner: Edge, Geo, Core, and Processing module owners
actions.rationale: Read-only reachability evidence shows independently built, imported, tested, or gated runtime boundaries. Names alone cannot justify deletion or merger.
actions.replacement: A separately approved R3 exact-import-graph and before/after build, contract, replay, and CI proof.

reachabilityAudit.before: Three distinct production-composition, reusable-native-runtime, and diagnostic-capture boundaries with separate targets and gates.
reachabilityAudit.after: UNCHANGED_R0_R2: all sources, CMake targets, tests, and CI jobs remain reachable.

reachabilityAudit.before: geo-core is a light local-frame/time/projection library; geo-spatial owns heavier CRS, raster, terrain, and vertical-reference operations.
reachabilityAudit.after: UNCHANGED_R0_R2: dependency direction and independent contract/golden coverage remain intact.

reachabilityAudit.before: Core owns durable Mission-plan lifecycle while the package owns deterministic coverage, geometry, terrain, and WPML algorithms.
reachabilityAudit.after: UNCHANGED_R0_R2: authority and algorithm boundaries remain separate and tested.

reachabilityAudit.before: Core owns request/projection authority, the change service owns calculations, and processing-controller owns worker orchestration.
reachabilityAudit.after: UNCHANGED_R0_R2: all three roles and their test reachability remain intact.

reachabilityAudit.before: The orchestrator imports leaf IFC, defect, and perception implementations through separately packaged dependencies and optional model gates.
reachabilityAudit.after: UNCHANGED_R0_R2: package, import, optional-extra, and test boundaries remain intact.

verification.claim: Schema, required candidate classifications, archive hashes, selected links, document status, media split, naming, required-versus-optional retained-source semantics, and final root hygiene passed.
Normalization contract regression: 6 passed, including the actual-manifest clean-clone case.

verification.command: uv run --locked mypy packages services tests tools
verification.claim: Python type safety passed for 472 source files.
Repository Python regression: 4679 passed, 24 skipped; warnings did not fail the gate.

verification.command: npm run lint; npx tsc --noEmit; npm test
verification.claim: Dashboard ESLint and TypeScript passed; Vitest passed 63 files and 578 tests.
Patch whitespace integrity passed after the retained-source correction.
Current phase-state YAML parsed successfully while normalization remained GATED for re-review.

Reviewer /root/normalization_strict_review@2026-09-04-attempt-2 passed all eight attachment criteria after first refuting and then verifying the clean-clone correction; naming remains PARTIAL and external gates remain unchanged.
R0-R2 changes no runtime or capability state and cannot close physical gates.
